name.text: Writing an inequality from a graph

questiontext.text:
The graph shows a boundary line with the unwanted side shaded.

[[jsxgraph width="360px" height="360px"]] (function () { function clip(P, a, b, c, s) { var out = [], i, p, q, fp, fq, t; for (i = 0; i < P.length; i++) { p = P[i]; q = P[(i + 1) % P.length]; fp = s * (a * p[0] + b * p[1] - c); fq = s * (a * q[0] + b * q[1] - c); if (fp >= 0) { out.push(p); } if ((fp >= 0) !== (fq >= 0)) { t = fp / (fp - fq); out.push([p[0] + t * (q[0] - p[0]), p[1] + t * (q[1] - p[1])]); } } return out; } function frame(x0, x1, y0, y1) { return [[x0, y0], [x1, y0], [x1, y1], [x0, y1]]; } function unwanted(L, R) { var s = (L[3] === 'lt' || L[3] === 'le') ? 1 : -1; return clip(R, L[0], L[1], L[2], s); } function shade(b, P) { if (P.length < 3) { return; } b.create('polygon', P, {fillColor: '#808080', fillOpacity: 0.3, borders: {strokeWidth: 0, visible: false}, vertices: {visible: false}, fixed: true, highlight: false, withLines: false, hasInnerPoints: false}); } function boundary(b, L, dashedOverride) { var strict = (L[3] === 'lt' || L[3] === 'gt'); if (dashedOverride !== undefined) { strict = dashedOverride; } // A dashed boundary on an axis (x = 0 or y = 0) would be hidden by the solid axis drawn // under it; a white line underneath breaks the axis so the dashes show. if (strict && L[2] === 0 && (L[0] === 0 || L[1] === 0)) { b.create('line', [0, L[0], L[1]], {strokeColor: '#ffffff', strokeWidth: 4, fixed: true, highlight: false}); } b.create('line', [-L[2], L[0], L[1]], {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 2, dash: strict ? 2 : 0, fixed: true, highlight: false, straightFirst: true, straightLast: true}); } function grid(b, x0, x1, y0, y1, step) { var g = {strokeColor: '#d0d0d0', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}, k, ax = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true, highlight: false, lastArrow: {type: 2, size: 6}}; for (k = Math.ceil(x0); k <= x1; k++) { b.create('segment', [[k, y0], [k, y1]], g); } for (k = Math.ceil(y0); k <= y1; k++) { b.create('segment', [[x0, k], [x1, k]], g); } b.create('arrow', [[x0, 0], [x1, 0]], ax); b.create('arrow', [[0, y0], [0, y1]], ax); var t = {fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 11, anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top'}; for (k = Math.ceil(x0); k < x1; k++) { if (k !== 0 && k % step === 0) { b.create('text', [k, -0.15, String(k)], t); } } for (k = Math.ceil(y0); k < y1; k++) { if (k !== 0 && k % step === 0) { b.create('text', [-0.2, k, String(k)], {fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 11, anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'middle'}); } } b.create('text', [-0.2, -0.15, '0'], {fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 11, anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'top'}); b.create('text', [x1 - 0.1, 0.25, 'x'], {fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 14, anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'bottom'}); b.create('text', [0.25, y1 - 0.1, 'y'], {fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 14, anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'top'}); } function opts(bb) { return {boundingbox: bb, keepAspectRatio: true, axis: false, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}; } var L = [{#a#}, {#b#}, {#c#}, {#rel#}], lo = {#blo#}, hi = {#bhi#}, st = {#bst#}; var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, opts([lo - 0.5, hi + 0.5, hi + 0.5, lo - 0.5])); var R = frame(lo, hi, lo, hi); grid(b, lo, hi, lo, hi, st); shade(b, unwanted(L, R)); boundary(b, L); // R at the area centroid of the clear part (the vertex average can sit on the origin's labels) var s = (L[3] === 'lt' || L[3] === 'le') ? -1 : 1, W = clip(R, L[0], L[1], L[2], s), cx = 0, cy = 0, ar = 0, cr, i, p, q; for (i = 0; i < W.length; i++) { p = W[i]; q = W[(i + 1) % W.length]; cr = p[0] * q[1] - q[0] * p[1]; ar += cr; cx += (p[0] + q[0]) * cr; cy += (p[1] + q[1]) * cr; } cx = cx / (3 * ar); cy = cy / (3 * ar); // then the half-unit grid point in the clear part that keeps clear of the axes and the line, nearest that centroid var nl = Math.sqrt(L[0] * L[0] + L[1] * L[1]), bx = cx, by = cy, bsc = -1e9, gx2, gy2, dd, sc2; for (gx2 = lo + 0.5; gx2 <= hi - 0.5; gx2 += 0.5) { for (gy2 = lo + 0.5; gy2 <= hi - 0.5; gy2 += 0.5) { dd = s * (L[0] * gx2 + L[1] * gy2 - L[2]) / nl; if (dd < 0.8) { continue; } dd = Math.min(dd, Math.abs(gx2) + 0.2, Math.abs(gy2) + 0.2, 1.5); sc2 = 10 * dd - Math.sqrt((gx2 - cx) * (gx2 - cx) + (gy2 - cy) * (gy2 - cy)); if (sc2 > bsc) { bsc = sc2; bx = gx2; by = gy2; } } } cx = bx; cy = by; b.create('text', [cx, cy, 'R'], {fixed: true, highlight: false, fontSize: 20, fontWeight: 'bold', anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle', cssStyle: 'font-weight:bold;'}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

Key: shaded, not wanted; unshaded (\(R\)), the required region.

The shaded region is not wanted. Write the inequality that describes the clear region \(R\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1, the boundary: the line crosses the axes at \(({@X@}, 0)\) and \((0, {@Y@})\), so its equation is {@lind(a, b, c)@} (check: \(x = {@X@}, y = 0\) gives \({@a*X@}\); \(x = 0, y = {@Y@}\) gives \({@b*Y@}\)).

Step 2, the style: the line is [[if test="strictp(rel)"]]dashed, so points on it are not in \(R\): use \(\lt\) or \(\gt\)[[else]]solid, so points on it are in \(R\): use \(\le\) or \(\ge\)[[/if]].

Step 3, the direction, from a point in the clear region: [[if test="oin"]]the origin is in \(R\), and at \((0, 0)\) the left side is \(0\), which is [[if test="is(c>0)"]]less[[else]]more[[/if]] than \({@c@}\).[[else]]the origin is in the shaded part, so \(R\) is the side where the left side is [[if test="is(c>0)"]]more[[else]]less[[/if]] than \({@c@}\) (at \((0, 0)\) it is \(0\)).[[/if]]

So \(R\) is {@ineqd(a, b, c, rel)@}. Any equivalent form is also right, for example with every term multiplied by the same positive number.

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: an inequality from a graph

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Write the inequality for the clear region of a graph with one sloping boundary, with the unwanted side shaded.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 1 (Graphing inequalities), Section C, question C5 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: new boundary lines, the unwanted side shaded and the clear region described.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

falsefeedback.text: The boundary is a sloping line, so your inequality needs both \(x\) and \(y\).

truefeedback.text: That describes the shaded side. The shaded side is the one we do not want: write the inequality for the clear region \(R\), and check it with a point in \(R\).

node.description: Sign the wrong way, same strictness

truefeedback.text: Your sign points towards the shaded side. Test a point in \(R\), then check whether the line is solid or dashed.
The direction is right. The line is [[if test="strictp(rel)"]]dashed, so use \(\lt\) or \(\gt\)[[else]]solid, so use \(\le\) or \(\ge\)[[/if]].
Check the boundary: it crosses the axes at \(({@X@}, 0)\) and \((0, {@Y@})\); yours crosses at \(({@Y@}, 0)\) and \((0, {@X@})\).

falsefeedback.text: [[if test="llin"]]Your inequality has {@lbd@} as its boundary, which is not the line on the graph. [[/if]]Find the equation of the line from where it crosses the axes, choose \(\le\), \(\lt\), \(\ge\) or \(\gt\) from its style, and test a point in \(R\).
